newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Resources unit launches HK's first PCS.
newsitem.headline: China Resources unit launches HK's first PCS.

text.p: Peoples Telephone Co Ltd, a unit of China Resources Holdings Co Ltd, launched Hong Kong's first personal communications services (PCS) system on Tuesday with expectations it could break even within three years.
"We expect to break even with 180,000 customers and this could be achieved in three years. We forecast to get our investments back in five years," managing director Michael Leung told reporters.
Peoples Telephone, one of six PCS providers granted a licence last September, planned to invest HK$2.4 billion to HK$2.7 billion in the new mobile phone system, he said.
"We already put in about HK$500-600 million and will invest another HK$500-600 million from now to mid-1998," Leung said.
The company would need to invest HK$1.2 billion to HK$1.5 billion between mid-1998 and 2000, he added.
China Resources, also the parent of locally listed China Resources Enterprise Ltd, holds a 54.5 percent stake in Peoples Telephone.
The other shareholders are Telepaging Ltd with 18 percent, Unisource with 22 percent and Mobile Systems International Plc with 5.5 percent.
Unisource groups telecoms operators Dutch PTT, Telia AB of Sweden, Swiss Telecom PTT and Spain's Telefonica.
Peoples Telephone has initially limited its service to Hong Kong's commercial centres and heavy populated areas, but said it would extend cover to most of the territory by the end of 1997.

The company has more than twice the government's required 40 base stations, and expected to have a very mature network with about 270 stations by the end of the year and 550 stations in two years, Leung said.
